title: Spanish Nationalists
capsule: The Nationalist faction (Bando nacional) was the coalition of Spanish Army officers, Falangists, Carlists, and monarchists who launched a coup against the Second Republic on 17–18 July 1936; Francisco Franco assumed supreme command (Generalísimo) in September 1936 after the deaths of Generals Sanjurjo and Mola. Nazi Germany contributed the Condor Legion — which bombed Guernica on 26 April 1937 — and Fascist Italy supplied approximately 75,000 troops at the campaign's peak. After nearly three years of fighting and roughly 500,000 deaths in all causes, Franco declared victory on 1 April 1939, establishing a dictatorship that endured until his death in November 1975.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial advance of the Nationalists is well documented month-by-month from military records and press reports; the dataset period 1936–1939 captures the Civil War phase precisely.
